subject: history
title: History MYP 5 Interactive Practice 1 (4 tasks, 28 marks)

questions.content:
[[Q 1 | A 5 | C 2]]
This task is about the causes of the First World War.
(a) Match each date to the event that happened on it. (4 marks)
{{drag|d1|28 June 1914,4 August 1914,11 November 1918,28 June 1919|Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated in Sarajevo,Britain declares war on Germany,The armistice ends the fighting on the Western Front,The Treaty of Versailles is signed,The Tsar of Russia abdicates}}
(b) The assassination in Sarajevo was the {{select|t1|long-term cause|trigger|consequence}} of the war. (1 mark)
(c) State two long-term causes of the war. (2 marks)

Total for Question 1: 7 marks
questions.mark_scheme: (a) Interactive answer [d1]: 28 June 1914 = Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated in Sarajevo [1]; 4 August 1914 = Britain declares war on Germany [1]; 11 November 1918 = the armistice ends the fighting on the Western Front [1]; 28 June 1919 = the Treaty of Versailles is signed [1]. 'The Tsar of Russia abdicates' is a distractor (it happened in 1917). (b) Interactive answer [t1] = trigger [1]. (c) Any two of: the alliance system, militarism and the arms race, imperial rivalry, nationalism [1] [1].

questions.content:
[[Q 2 | A 4 | C 3]]
This task is about the Treaty of Versailles of 1919.
(a) Match each theme to the term of the treaty. (3 marks)
{{drag|v1|War guilt,Army,Territory|Germany accepted responsibility for causing the war,The German army was limited to 100 000 men,Alsace-Lorraine was returned to France,Germany became a member of the League of Nations in 1920}}
(b) The League of Nations was created to {{select|l1|keep peace between countries|collect taxes|run schools}}. (1 mark)
(c) Explain why many Germans resented the treaty. (3 marks)

Total for Question 2: 7 marks
questions.mark_scheme: (a) Interactive answer [v1]: War guilt = Germany accepted responsibility for causing the war [1]; Army = the German army was limited to 100 000 men [1]; Territory = Alsace-Lorraine was returned to France [1]. The League of Nations item is a distractor (Germany joined later, in 1926). (b) Interactive answer [l1] = keep peace between countries [1]. (c) Identifies a term Germans resented such as the war guilt clause, limits on the army, loss of territory or reparations [1]; develops with detail or an example [1]; explains the link to resentment, for example that Germany was not allowed to negotiate so the treaty was seen as dictated and humiliating [1].

(a) Interactive answer [y1]: plotted (3, 1), (3, 2), (4, 3), (5, 4), (6, 5); all five correct [1] (the Russian Revolution and the USA entering the war both fall 3 years after 1914, which is 1917). (b) Interactive answer [y2] rows: (Armistice, 1918) [1]; (Treaty of Versailles, 1919) [1]; (League of Nations first meets, 1920) [1]. (c) Allied armies and economies were tired after years of fighting [1]; the USA brought fresh troops and supplies [1]; this shifted the balance of resources against Germany and helped lead to the armistice in 1918 [1].

questions.content:
[[Q 4 | D 5 | C 2]]
A student states: 'The assassination in Sarajevo was the only cause of the First World War.'
(a) Choose the statement that best matches the view of most historians. The assassination was {{select|j1|the only cause|one of several causes}} of the war. (1 mark)
(b) Evaluate the student's statement. Use at least three factors in your answer and reach a supported judgement. (6 marks)

Total for Question 4: 7 marks
questions.mark_scheme: (a) Interactive answer [j1] = one of several causes [1]. (b) Award marks for: the assassination on 28 June 1914 as the immediate trigger [1]; the alliance system pulling other powers into the conflict [1]; militarism or the arms race [1]; nationalism or imperial rivalry [1]; an explicit judgement that long-term tensions made the trigger so serious [1]; a justified conclusion, for example that without these tensions the assassination might have stayed a local crisis [1].
